children: Former Treasury Secretary
Jack Lew
said lawmakers should begin addressing Social Security’s funding challenges before the program reaches its projected exhaustion date.

Lew made the comments during an interview on CNBC’s "The Exchange" on Thursday, saying Social Security will run out of enough current income to fully pay current benefits during the term of the next president.
Social Security Reform
"There are solutions, but the solutions get harder and harder as you get closer to the exhaustion date. So it’s not too soon to start thinking and talking about it," Lew said.

"I would certainly caution anyone running for president the next time or running for the Senate to keep their options open, because it’s going to take something along the lines of a 1983 approach where you do something serious to address solvency."
A 1983-Style Approach
Lew said the 1983 effort was bipartisan and involved an indirect negotiation between the “president and the Congress," with Congress controlled by a different party.
